nasa-shared-service-cent-stennis-space-c.note: The Title V permit 1000-00054 for the NASA Shared Services Center at Stennis lists 9 emergency diesel generators. Six are 2,000 kilowatts and three are 3,250 kilowatts, which sums to 21.75 MW. The permit gives kilowatts beside the horsepower figures but does not label them electrical. That is below the 50 MW threshold.

amazon-canton.note: The Mississippi permit 1720-00098 agrees with GEM Unit 1 at 326 generators, 896.5 MW. It also lists 10 small generators, 7.8 MW, that GEM lacks, so I propose them as a new unit.

compass-meridian.note: Permit 1460-00133 lists 420 generators and 813 MW, which agrees with GEM's two unit rows. The harvest's 60 engines for Building 1 is a reading error.

amazon-ridgeland.note: Permit 1720-00099 lists 391 generators and 1,060 MW, which agrees with GEM's three unit rows apart from rounding 4.05 MW to 4.1.

mzt-tech-llc-100-southaven.note: Permit 0680-00119 covers 41 permanent turbines, 1,240.5 MW, which agrees with Unit 2. The temporary turbines in Unit 1 are outside the permit. It has no emergency engines.

amazon-clinton.note: A September 2026 public notice and the state permit database show a data center at 1001 Industrial Park Drive in Clinton with back-up generators of about 250 MW, owned by Amazon Data Services. I did not find the draft permit, so the generator count is blank.
